en.title: Diphthongs in One Syllable
en.summary: Learn how two vowels glide together to form one single syllable.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: A syllable is one beat of a word. A vowel is a sound with open air and no mouth touch. A diphthong means two vowel sounds that glide together in one syllable. Your mouth changes shape without any pause between them. Listen to (ploaie) /ˈplo̯a.je/, which means rain. You hear two vowels in the first beat.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start with your lips in one shape. Let the air leave your mouth with your voice on. Then move your lips smoothly into the next shape. Do not stop the voice between the two sounds. Say the first part of (ploaie) /ˈplo̯a.je/ as one single push of air. Keep the movement very smooth and quick.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look at the letters on the page. A letter is a sign of the alphabet. Two vowel letters often sit next to each other in one syllable. They show that you must glide the sounds together. In the word (ploaie) /ˈplo̯a.je/, the first two vowel letters make one beat. You read them together as one sound unit.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not split the two vowels into two separate beats. If you pause, you create two syllables instead of one. Do not say (ploaie) /ˈplo̯a.je/ with three beats. The first two vowels belong to the same beat. Move your tongue and lips smoothly. Keep the sound unbroken from start to end.
